meaning.failureMeaning:
Adapter activation and readiness race their operation against a timer and can reject with ADAPTER_START_TIMEOUT. Overall shutdown races against ADAPTER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT. These rejections and abort signals do not prove that the underlying adapter work stopped. 

Readiness teardown, rollback and late activation cleanup pass an abort signal. They still await the shutdown promise. An adapter that ignores cancellation can keep that cleanup pending. Stop before declaring cleanup complete or replaying an uncertain effect.

meaning.text:
Selects the base URL for Prism design-set and revision POST operations. A truthy configured value overrides the environment and built-in fallback.

Accepted values: string with no narrower scalar constraint. The schema accepts any string. The consumer uses new URL to resolve the operation path against the selected base. The post function adds no protocol restriction or timeout.

Omission: With no truthy configured controlUrl and a truthy PRISM_CONTROL_URL value, the consumer uses that environment value. With no truthy value from either source, the consumer uses http://127.0.0.1:28080. A truthy configured controlUrl takes precedence over both.

Empty value: An empty string is schema-valid and falls through to the environment value or built-in base. Null is not schema-valid.

Change effect: When the Prism OpenClaw design-control client next loads the configuration, a change to $.controlUrl has the effect given above.

Failure: An invalid base fails in new URL before fetch. Network or protocol errors can make fetch fail. With response.ok false, post evaluates ``new Error(value.error || `Prism control returned HTTP ${response.status}`)``. With a null JSON value, value.error access can fail before that Error is constructed. Failed JSON parsing gives HTTP plus the response status. The post function adds no request timeout.
